title: Quick Tri-Dal
subtitle: A light, everyday tempered dal — toor, urad, and chana, no soaking required.
protein: ~10–12g protein per adult serving — from toor, urad & chana dal

method.title: Rinse and pressure-cook the dals
items: Rinse {@toor}, {@urad} and {@chana} together under water until it runs mostly clear — no soaking needed
Add to the pressure cooker with {@water:cook}, {@turmeric} and {@salt}
Pressure cook 6–7 whistles on medium heat — the extra whistle or two makes up for skipping the soak, especially for the chana dal
Let pressure release naturally, then whisk lightly with a ladle until the dal is smooth but still has a little texture

method.label: Toddler — pull before the tempering
items: Scoop out a small bowl (about ¾ cup) of the plain cooked dal now, before tempering
Stir in a small pat of {@ghee-toddler:toddler} for richness — her bowl stays plain and mild since it's set aside before the chili-spiced tempering is made

method.title: Make the tempering (tadka)
items: Heat {@ghee} in a small pan over medium heat
Add {@hing} and {@ginger}, sauté 20–30 seconds until fragrant
Add {@chili-powder}, stir for just a few seconds so it doesn't scorch

method.title: Finish, then store for meal prep
items: Pour the hot tempering over the remaining dal (the toddler portion has already been set aside) and stir well
Adjust consistency with {@water:adjust} — this dal should be pourable, not thick like a gravy
Simmer 3–4 minutes on low heat so the flavors settle
Garnish servings with {@cilantro} just before eating — store the rest without it
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate in an airtight container — keeps 4 days
Reheat on the stovetop with a splash of water to loosen; add the garnish fresh after reheating

method.label: Notes
method.text: Stovetop pressure cooker works straight from rinsed dal — no soak needed since these are all split and dehusked; give it one or two extra whistles versus a soaked-dal recipe to make sure the chana dal fully softens. Chana dal is optional — skip it and use 1 cup toor dal + ½ cup urad dal instead (same total volume), dropping back to 5–6 whistles. This is a thinner, everyday dal, not a gravy — meant for rice or roti as a daily-rotation option alongside the richer dal makhani. Ginger is added generously here since it's the main warming element in a light, Jain dal like this.
